Cutover map

Every section of the business and who is master of it today. Computyme ends up running warehouse distribution only; everything else moves to PIV2 one section at a time. Sections the B2B site reads are marked, because nothing there moves without a check.

How a section cuts over

  1. Show it as it is. While Computyme is master, PIV2 reads it from the EDA mirror and shows it locked. Nothing is written back.
  2. Extend it. Anything Computyme doesn't have is added in PIV2 as an extension, so the work starts before the switch.
  3. Reconcile. PIV2 compares SQL with Computyme and lists every mismatch for a person to decide. Nothing is overwritten automatically in either direction.
  4. Flip only when they match. That comparison is the check before the switch: the section moves to SQL only when SQL matches Computyme, and the change is logged here with who and why.
  5. Keep Computyme fed. Where Computyme still reads the data (warehouse, billing, payables), PIV2 sends it back until that part moves too.
